items.title: 15.3.3 Use of the retardation factor (Rf value ka istemal) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 15.3.3 with the Rf equations, Figure 15.10 and the Whatman paper box, printed page 331.

blocks.text: Har component ka apna khaas retardation factor (component kitna peeche reh gaya, us ka number) hota hai jise Rf value kehte hain. Rf value yun nikalti hai:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein ek jagah 'Rr value' chhapa hai; sahi 'Rf value' hai.

blocks.latex: R_f = \frac{\text{Distance travelled by a component from the original spot}}{\text{Distance travelled by solvent from the original spot}}
blocks.text_alt: Rf = Distance travelled by a component from the original spot / Distance travelled by solvent from the original spot

blocks.title: Easy words mein
blocks.text: Dono distances (faasle) ek hi jagah se naape jate hain: asal spot wali pencil lakeer (base line) se. Component kabhi solvent se aage nahi jata, is liye Rf hamesha 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hota hai aur is ki koi unit nahi hoti.
Figure 15.10 ka chromatogram dikhata hai ke sample A mein B aur C dono components hain. B aur C ki Rf values yeh hain:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki picture mein distances par sirf '1' chhapa hai (ek distance to do spots ke beech naapa gaya hai), aur text mein Rf(B) aur Rf(C) dono ko x/y likha hai. Sahi yeh hai: har distance base line se naapa jata hai; B (neela spot) ka distance x aur C (kaala spot) ka distance x' hai, is liye Rf(B) = x/y aur Rf(C) = x'/y.

blocks.alt: Teen samples A, B aur C ka chromatogram. A mein ek kaala (oopar) aur ek neela (neeche) spot; B mein sirf neela, C mein sirf kaala. y base line se solvent front tak distance; x aur x' base line se neele aur kaale spot tak distances.
blocks.caption: Figure 15.10: Chromatogram (kitab ki Figure 15.10 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: A ke dono spots B aur C ke spots ki seedh mein hain, is liye A impure hai aur us mein B aur C dono hain. y base line se solvent front tak ka distance hai; x neele spot tak aur x' kaale spot tak.

Paper chromatography se aasani se pata chalta hai ke chemical reaction mein bana substance pure hai ya impure, bas aisa solvent lena hota hai jis mein substance hal ho jaye. Pure substance chromatogram par ek spot deta hai, jabke impure substance ek se zyada spots deta hai.

Paper chromatogram se substances ko pehchana bhi ja sakta hai: unhen pure substances ke known (maloom) samples se mila kar dekha jata hai. Jin do substances ki Rf values barabar hon, woh shayad ek hi substance hain.

blocks.title: Interesting Information (dilchasp maloomat)
blocks.text: Paper chromatography mein istemal hone wala Whatman filter paper khaas chune hue cotton cellulose se banta hai. Whatman filter paper No. 1 aam kaam ke liye hai; is ki retention (particles rokne ki ability) aur flow rate (behne ki speed) medium (darmiyani) hai. Is ke pores ka size 11 μm hai.

Figure 15.10 ke chromatogram mein impure substance mein do components hain, kyun ke us ne do rangeen spots diye hain. Impure substance ke spots utna hi distance chale hain jitna reference ke pure compounds. Agar stationary phase aur mobile phase wahi rahen to kisi substance ki Rf value hamesha ek jaisi rehti hai.

blocks.caption: Chromatogram parhna
rows: known pure sample jaisi Rf par spot

blocks.prompt: Ek component base line se 3.0 cm chala aur solvent front 6.0 cm. Rf value kya hai?
blocks.explanation: Rf = component ka distance ÷ solvent ka distance = 3.0 cm ÷ 6.0 cm = 0.5. Dono distances base line se naape jate hain; units cancel ho jati hain.

blocks.prompt: Rf value aur us ka istemal explain karein. Agar do components stationary phase se taqreeban barabar chipakte hon to kya hoga?
blocks.explanation: Rf = component ka distance ÷ solvent front ka distance, dono base line se. Wahi phases hon to kisi substance ki Rf hamesha ek rehti hai, is liye is se substance pehchana jata hai aur purity jaanchi jati hai (pure substance = ek spot). Agar do components barabar chipakte hon to woh taqreeban ek speed se chalte hain aur un ke spots ek doosre par aa jate hain; unhen alag karne ke liye solvent badalna parta hai.

items: Rf = component ka distance ÷ solvent front ka distance (dono base line se); Rf 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan, koi unit nahi.
Wahi phases mein substance ki Rf hamesha wahi; ek spot = pure, zyada spots = impure; known sample se Rf mila kar substance pehchana jata hai.
